headline: Park City Mountain and Regional Activity Bookings
reservation: Reservations for ski lift access, local equipment rentals, and high-season dining should be made well in advance, particularly during festival windows and winter holidays. While the town is public, specific resorts like Deer Valley or Park City Mountain have independent ticketing systems. Check official resort portals for current seasonal access policies.

days.title: Mountain Peaks and Main Street
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from Salt Lake City

stops.name: Park City Mountain
stops.detail: Access the high-altitude terrain via seasonal lift rides for hiking or skiing.

stops.name: Historic Main Street
stops.detail: Walk through the former silver mining hub, now featuring local galleries and boutiques.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes from SLC; winter conditions can significantly increase travel time.
days.note: Altitude effects may be felt; stay hydrated and pace movement during the first day.

days.title: Olympic Legacies and Alpine Lakes

stops.name: Utah Olympic Park
stops.detail: Visit the Olympic winter-sports venue to see the jumps and museum exhibits.

stops.name: Jordanelle State Park
stops.detail: A nearby reservoir offering paddleboarding and scenic water views against the Wasatch Range.

days.driving: Short local transfers; allow 20 minutes between the Olympic Park and Jordanelle.
days.note: Reservoir access and water activities are seasonal; check state park status for closures.

days.title: High Alpine Passes

stops.name: Guardsman Pass
stops.detail: Drive the scenic mountain pass for expansive views of the surrounding valleys and peaks.

stops.name: Blood Lake Trail
stops.detail: A popular high-elevation hike accessible from the pass area for alpine scenery.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for the winding climb; road is subject to seasonal winter closure.
days.note: Parking at the pass is extremely limited; arrive early or utilize local shuttle options if available.

intel.title: Resort and Town Logistics
intel.text: Main Street parking is limited and typically requires payment. Use the Richardson Flat park-and-ride for easier access to the town center via local transit.

intel.title: Mountain Coverage
intel.text: Reliable signal exists in town, but coverage drops quickly in the Uinta National Forest and on high-alpine trails. Carry a physical map for backcountry exploration.

intel.title: High Valley Services
intel.text: Major fueling stations are concentrated along the S.R. 224 corridor and in nearby Heber City. Remote mountain roads have no services.

intel.title: Seasonal Transitions
intel.text: The 'mud season' in late spring can result in closed trails to protect local soil. Winter travelers should monitor the snow report for lift operation changes.

intel.title: Guardsman Pass Status
intel.text: The pass connecting Park City to Big Cottonwood Canyon is closed by snow for much of the year. Check UDOT for official seasonal opening dates.

plan.arrival: Collect rental at Salt Lake City (SLC), then proceed east on I-80. Stock up at Kimball Junction before heading to mountain accommodations.
plan.vehicle: A 4WD or AWD vehicle with winter tires is strongly recommended for winter travel; check rental agency snow policies.
plan.goldenHour: Empire Pass provides a notable vantage for sunset views over the Wasatch, depending on cloud cover and season.
